meta.name: Freight Invoice Audit Agent
meta.one_liner: AI agent that audits freight invoices against contracts and recovers the 2-5% shippers overpay.
meta.evaluator: Claude (evaluate-startup) — ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE, all data fictional

idea.description: Mid-market shippers (50-500 shipments/week) routinely overpay freight carriers due to billing errors: wrong accessorial charges, misapplied contract rates, duplicate invoices. Large enterprises employ audit firms; mid-market firms eat the loss. The agent ingests carrier invoices and rate contracts, flags discrepancies with evidence, and drafts dispute claims for human approval.
idea.target_customer: Logistics or finance manager at a mid-market shipper with 50-500 shipments/week and no dedicated audit staff.
idea.value_proposition: Recover 2-5% of freight spend with near-zero effort: forward invoices, approve flagged disputes, collect refunds.
idea.founder_context: Solo technical founder, 8 years backend/ML, no logistics background but a warm contact at two regional shippers. Bootstrapping, 20 h/week alongside consulting.

interview_notes.q: Walk me through the moment someone hits this problem.
interview_notes.a: AP clerk gets a 40-line carrier invoice, has no time to check line items against the rate contract PDF, approves it. Errors surface only in annual audits, if ever.

interview_notes.q: Have you seen anyone pay to work around this?
interview_notes.a: Enterprises pay audit firms 30-50% contingency on recovered amounts. Mid-market firms told me the firms won't take them - too small.
That contract parsing is too messy - every carrier contract is a differently-scanned PDF with amendments.

angles.title: Market size & demand
angles.summary: US mid-market freight audit is a genuinely underserved slice of a large spend pool; incumbent audit firms concentrate on enterprise contingency deals, leaving smaller shippers with no realistic option.
findings: US business freight spend is measured in the high hundreds of billions annually; even fractions of a percent in billing errors represent a large recoverable pool (estimate).
Industry rules of thumb place freight invoice error rates between 2% and 5% of spend (estimate, multiple secondary sources).
Traditional audit firms typically require enterprise-scale volume, quoting minimums that exclude sub-500-shipments/week shippers.
No dominant self-serve software product for contract-vs-invoice freight audit surfaced in searches; adjacent TMS platforms treat audit as a checkbox feature.

sources.title: Freight audit firm service pages (illustrative)
sources.note: Supports contingency pricing and enterprise minimums

angles.title: Competitors & alternatives
angles.summary: Competition is real but oblique: contingency audit firms (enterprise-only), TMS suites with shallow audit modules, and spreadsheets. Nobody owns the mid-market wedge with a product-shaped offer.
findings: Contingency audit firms are the strongest analog and validate willingness to pay a revenue share for recovered money.
TMS vendors could add deeper audit features, but their incentive is carrier-relationship-neutral workflow software, not adversarial auditing.
The credible fast-follower threat is another AI startup, not an incumbent.

angles.title: Technology & state of the art
angles.summary: Invoice extraction is a solved problem at high accuracy; heterogeneous contract parsing (scanned PDFs, amendments, rate tables) is the hard 20% and the de-facto moat if cracked for the long tail of carrier formats.
findings: Modern document AI reliably extracts line items from standard carrier invoice formats.
Rate contracts are the messy side: multi-document amendments, embedded tables, carrier-specific accessorial codes.
The audit computation itself (rate x lane x weight vs. billed) is deterministic once both sides are structured - ideal verifiability.

categories.name: Problem & Demand
categories.summary: Quantified, recurring money leak with proven willingness to pay a share of recovery - but the pain is silent (victims often don't know), which raises the education burden.

dimensions.name: Pain intensity
dimensions.rationale: Direct, quantifiable financial loss; 2-5% of a core cost line is CFO-visible once surfaced.

dimensions.name: Frequency & urgency
dimensions.rationale: Every invoice cycle, continuously; urgency is low only because the loss is invisible.

dimensions.name: Problem specificity
dimensions.rationale: Crisply nameable: billed amount deviates from contracted amount.

dimensions.name: Demand evidence
dimensions.rationale: Enterprises demonstrably pay contingency auditors; mid-market willingness inferred, not yet observed.

sources.title: Freight audit firm service pages (illustrative)
sources.note: Contingency model proves payment for recovery

categories.name: Market & Timing
categories.summary: Comfortable niche rather than venture-scale headline; timing is good because document AI just crossed the accuracy bar that makes long-tail contract parsing economical.

dimensions.name: Reachable market
dimensions.rationale: Mid-market shipper audit is plausibly a low-hundreds-of-millions serviceable pool - solid for a focused company, not a land grab.

dimensions.name: Growth trajectory
dimensions.rationale: Freight complexity and accessorial proliferation trend upward, growing the error surface.

dimensions.name: Why now
dimensions.rationale: Contract-grade document AI became cheap enough to serve customers audit firms reject.

dimensions.name: Tailwinds
dimensions.rationale: Margin pressure in logistics helps; no regulatory forcing function either way.

categories.name: Solution & Automation Leverage
categories.summary: Near-ideal agentic shape: deterministic verification core, cheap errors, fast feedback, clean decomposition. The one soft spot is getting clean contract data in.

dimensions.name: Outcome verifiability
dimensions.rationale: Billed-vs-contracted is arithmetic once parsed; carrier accept/reject of disputes is a binary external ground truth.

dimensions.name: Error tolerance
dimensions.rationale: False positive costs a 5-minute human review before filing; no irreversible action is automated.

dimensions.name: Feedback loop speed
dimensions.rationale: Parsing errors surface immediately; dispute outcomes return in days to weeks.

dimensions.name: Scope decomposability
dimensions.rationale: Month-audit → invoice → line item → field extraction; each level independently checkable, errors caught before rolling up.

dimensions.name: Data & context availability
dimensions.rationale: Invoices arrive by email/EDI; contracts exist but as heterogeneous PDFs - accessible, messy.

categories.name: Competition & Moat
categories.summary: Wedge is open today, but durable defense must be earned: the carrier-format parsing corpus and dispute-outcome dataset compound, everything else is copyable.

dimensions.name: Competitive intensity
dimensions.rationale: No direct mid-market product found, but adjacent players abound and the idea is discoverable.

dimensions.name: Differentiation
dimensions.rationale: 10x on access (serving the rejected segment) more than on capability.

dimensions.name: Defensibility
dimensions.rationale: Parsing corpus across carrier formats + dispute win-rate data are the only compounding assets; both take time.

dimensions.name: Platform risk
dimensions.rationale: TMS vendors could bundle audit, but adversarial auditing conflicts with their carrier-neutral positioning.

categories.name: Business & Economics
categories.summary: Contingency pricing (share of recovered money) aligns incentives, prices itself, and converts skeptics; margins hinge on automating the contract-onboarding cost per customer.

dimensions.name: Revenue clarity
dimensions.rationale: Take 20-30% of recovered amounts - the enterprise-proven model, self-justifying ROI.

dimensions.name: Unit economics
dimensions.rationale: Marginal audit cost is near-zero compute; per-customer contract onboarding is the real COGS.

dimensions.name: Scalability
dimensions.rationale: Each new carrier format parsed benefits all customers; revenue scales with processed spend, not headcount.

dimensions.name: Capital intensity
dimensions.rationale: Bootstrappable to first revenue, but contingency model delays cash collection by the dispute cycle.

categories.name: Execution & Fit
categories.summary: Technically well-matched solo founder with real but thin domain access; part-time capacity and enterprise-ish sales cycles are the honest constraints.

dimensions.name: Technical feasibility
dimensions.rationale: Core pipeline buildable with current document AI; long-tail contract formats are grind, not research.

dimensions.name: MVP effort
dimensions.rationale: Single-carrier, single-customer manual-assist audit demonstrable in 4-6 weeks at 20 h/week.

dimensions.name: Founder advantage
dimensions.rationale: Strong builder profile; two warm shipper contacts but no logistics operating history or distribution.

dimensions.name: Regulatory & dependency drag
dimensions.rationale: No licensing required; dependency is carrier cooperation on disputes, which contingency firms prove is workable.

verdict.summary: A textbook agentic wedge: deterministic verification core, contained errors, contingency pricing that sells itself - aimed at a segment incumbents structurally ignore. Attractiveness is capped by niche market size and an earnable-but-not-yet-earned moat. Build the smallest honest test: one carrier, one shipper, manual-assist audit of one month of invoices.
strengths: Outcome verifiability is near-perfect: billed-vs-contracted arithmetic plus binary carrier accept/reject ground truth.
Contingency pricing removes the buying decision - customers only pay from money they didn't know they'd lost.
Mid-market is structurally rejected by incumbent audit firms, not merely underserved.
Errors are cheap and contained: every automated flag passes a 5-minute human review before any external action.
weaknesses: Silent pain: prospects don't know they're bleeding, so top-of-funnel requires proof-first selling (e.g. free retro-audit).
Moat is prospective - the parsing corpus and dispute dataset only compound after meaningful volume.
Solo founder at 20 h/week vs. a grind-heavy long tail of contract formats.
Niche ceiling: strong cash business, unlikely venture-scale story without adjacent expansion.

risks.risk: Contract parsing accuracy stalls below the trust threshold on messy scanned amendments
risks.mitigation: Human-in-the-loop contract onboarding initially; treat parsing corpus as the product asset.

risks.risk: Carriers stonewall disputes from a software vendor without audit-firm standing
risks.mitigation: File disputes in the customer's name with evidence packets; measure accept-rate from customer one.

risks.risk: A funded AI competitor takes the same wedge with a sales team
risks.mitigation: Speed to referenceable recoveries; publish recovery benchmarks to own the category narrative.

risks.risk: Founder capacity: 20 h/week stretches MVP-to-revenue past 6 months and morale breaks
risks.mitigation: Scope MVP to one carrier format; pre-commit a go/no-go date.

assumptions.assumption: Mid-market shippers exhibit the same 2-5% error rate reported for enterprise freight
assumptions.current_evidence: Secondary-source rules of thumb only; no primary mid-market data found.

assumptions.assumption: A retro-audit of past invoices converts skeptical prospects at meaningful rates
assumptions.current_evidence: Untested; analog is contingency firms' free-audit sales motion.

assumptions.assumption: Two warm shipper contacts convert into design-partner access to real invoices and contracts
assumptions.current_evidence: Verbal interest expressed; nothing shared yet.

kill_criteria: Retro-audit of two real customers' invoices finds under 1% recoverable spend.
Carrier dispute acceptance rate below 30% after 20 evidence-backed filings.
Contract onboarding cannot be pushed below ~2 hours of human effort per carrier after 10 carriers.

validation_plan.question: Is the error rate real in mid-market?
validation_plan.method: Free manual retro-audit of 1 month of invoices for both warm contacts
validation_plan.success_signal: >=2% of audited spend flagged with defensible evidence

validation_plan.question: Will carriers pay out?
validation_plan.method: File the top 10 flagged disputes in customer's name with evidence packets

validation_plan.question: Will strangers buy?
validation_plan.method: Cold-outreach 30 mid-market shippers offering the free retro-audit

next_steps: Get written data-sharing agreement from both warm shipper contacts.
Build extraction pipeline for their primary carrier's invoice + contract format only.
Run the manual-assist retro-audit; hand-verify every flag.
File disputes for verified flags; instrument acceptance tracking.
Decision gate at week 8 against the kill criteria above.
